components.title: The difference: the model writes out its reasoning
components.reason: Two prompting methods compared on the same attributes.

items.name: Standard prompting
items.summary: Exemplars are plain question–answer pairs; the model answers directly.

citation.quote: in which a language model is given in-context exemplars of input–output pairs before outputting a prediction for a test-time example
The model gives the answer directly, as shown in Figure 1 (left).

items.name: Chain-of-thought prompting
items.summary: Each exemplar shows the reasoning before the answer, and the model imitates it.

citation.quote: Our proposed approach is to augment each exemplar in few-shot prompting with a chain of thought for an associated answer

attributes.value: Intermediate reasoning steps, then the answer

citation.quote: A chain of thought is a series of intermediate natural language reasoning steps that lead to the final output
so they have 3 + 6 = 9. The answer is 9.

components.title: How to build a chain-of-thought prompt
components.reason: Building the prompt is an ordered procedure.

steps.title: Pick a few exemplars
steps.detail: Write a handful of questions like the ones you want solved. The paper used eight exemplars for its math benchmarks.

steps.title: Write out the reasoning
steps.detail: For each exemplar, write the intermediate steps in plain language that lead to the answer.

steps.title: End with the answer
steps.detail: Finish every exemplar with the final answer, e.g. "The answer is 11."

steps.title: Append the new question
steps.detail: Put the test question last. The model continues the pattern: its own chain of thought, then the answer.
